theme.title: Warriors vs Cavaliers
theme.subtitle: The 2015 and 2017 Finals
theme.recap: Golden State won the first and third of four straight Finals meetings, with both sides setting records along the way.

questions.prompt: Counting the playoffs, how many games did the 2014–15 Warriors win?
questions.context: Golden State Warriors · 2014–15 · regular season plus playoffs

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Combining regular season and playoff games, Golden State finished 83–20

funFacts.text: Golden State's championship ended a drought dating to 1975, long before the Splash Brothers were born.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: winning their first championship since 1975, and fourth overall

funFacts.text: Steve Kerr became the first rookie head coach to win an NBA title since Pat Riley.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Kerr became the first rookie coach to win a title since Pat Riley

funFacts.text: That Warriors roster won the championship despite having no players with prior NBA Finals experience.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Warriors were the first team since the 1990–91 Bulls to win a title with a roster that did not have any players with Finals experience

questions.prompt: Andre Iguodala won 2015 Finals MVP. How many of the 11 votes did he get?
questions.note: Seven. The other four went to LeBron James of the losing Cavaliers.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Iguodala received seven out 11 votes; the other four went to James

funFacts.text: Iguodala became the first Finals MVP to win the award without starting every game of the series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He became the first and only player to win the award without starting every game of the series

funFacts.text: He was assigned to guard LeBron James, who shot a much lower percentage while Iguodala was on the court.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Iguodala was also tasked with guarding Cleveland star LeBron James, who made only 38.1% of his shots

funFacts.text: Kerr shifted Iguodala into the starting lineup for Game 4, with Draymond Green sliding to center.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Kerr inserted Andre Iguodala into the starting lineup in place of Andrew Bogut, while moving Draymond Green to the center position

questions.prompt: In Game 2 of the 2015 Finals, Stephen Curry set a Finals record for missed threes. How many?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Curry set an NBA record for most missed three-point attempts in an NBA Finals game with 13.

funFacts.text: Matthew Dellavedova's physical defense held Curry scoreless from the field on his attempts against him.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Matthew Dellavedova's defense on Curry was huge as Curry was 0–for–8 against him

funFacts.text: The overtime victory was Cleveland's first Finals game win in franchise history, after its earlier sweep in 2007.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The victory for Cleveland was their first ever single game Finals victory

funFacts.text: LeBron dubbed the undermanned Cavs 'The Grit Squad' as injuries forced a slower, tougher style.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: James had dubbed the undermanned Cavaliers as "The Grit Squad"

questions.prompt: Facing a sweep in 2017, Cleveland set a Finals record for points in a quarter. How many?
questions.note: 49 in the first quarter of Game 4.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Cleveland scored 49 points in the first quarter, the most points of any period in an NBA Finals game

funFacts.text: Cleveland's Game 4 victory ended Golden State's bid for a completely unbeaten postseason.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Warriors won the first three games, giving them a 15–0 record

funFacts.text: The Warriors–Cavaliers trilogy was the first time the same clubs played three consecutive NBA Finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the first time in NBA history that the same two teams played in three consecutive Finals

funFacts.text: Kevin Durant earned the Finals MVP award unanimously after his first championship series with the Warriors.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Kevin Durant was unanimously voted the NBA Finals Most Valuable Player

questions.prompt: LeBron James scored 44 points in Game 1 of the 2015 Finals. How many shots did he take?
questions.context: 2015 NBA Finals · Game 1 · at Golden State

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: James had a career NBA Finals high of 44 points, while attempting a postseason career-high 38 shots

funFacts.text: Kyrie Irving blocked a potential go-ahead Stephen Curry layup late in Game 1's regulation.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Curry beat Kyrie Irving to the basket and went for a go-ahead layup, but Irving blocked the shot

funFacts.text: The Cavaliers' offense scored just one basket in overtime, and Golden State took the series opener.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Cleveland's only score in the extra period was James' layup

funFacts.text: Irving fractured his left kneecap during overtime, joining injured Kevin Love on Cleveland's sideline.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: he was diagnosed with a fractured left kneecap that would require surgery and was ruled out for the rest of the Finals
